# Project Based Learning

 

A list of programming tutorials in which aspiring software developers learn how to build an application from scratch. These tutorials are divided into different primary programming languages. Tutorials may involve multiple technologies and languages.

To get started, simply fork this repo. Please refer to [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for contribution guidelines.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A curated index of highly practical programming tutorials focused strictly on building complete applications from scratch.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Project Based Learning is a comprehensive educational repository that indexes high-quality programming tutorials designed to teach through practical application development. Rather than focusing on abstract language syntax, the repository categorizes tutorials that guide learners step-by-step in constructing fully functional software projects. It spans dozens of languages and features complex builds like custom operating systems, network protocols, game engines, and production-ready web servers. The repository mandates that all included materials result in a tangible, working artifact, effectively bridging the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical engineering.
keyFeatures: Extensive language categorization: Organizes complex tutorials across dozens of primary programming languages from C++ to Rust.
Tangible project outcomes: Curates specifically for resources that result in a fully functioning software application rather than isolated exercises.
Advanced systems coverage: Includes systems-level tutorials for building network stacks, raw graphics renderers, and custom compilers.
Community vetted quality standards: Enforces strict contribution guidelines to ensure included tutorials are highly accurate, maintained, and genuinely educational.
Cross-disciplinary integration: Highlights projects that inherently require the integration of multiple unfamiliar technologies and architectural patterns.
Progressive skill mapping: Offers a huge range of projects scaling from basic command-line tools to building a functional Linux debugger.

useCases.description: Junior engineers systematically follow the web development guides to construct complex, highly customized applications they can showcase to employers.

useCases.title: Language Familiarization
useCases.description: Polyglot programmers rapidly learn the specific nuances of Rust or Go by immediately building a complex, real-world API server instead of reading syntax manuals.

useCases.title: Network Protocol Deconstruction
useCases.description: Security researchers follow the TCP/IP stack tutorials to practically understand and manipulate raw networking fundamentals from scratch.
